details: The latest US core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data for May showed a 3.4% year-over-year increase, the highest since October 2023. This higher-than-expected inflation has reduced expectations for imminent Federal Reserve rate cuts and increased the likelihood of future rate hikes, with some analysts now forecasting multiple hikes in 2026. In response, Bitcoin fell to an intraday low of $58,000 on Thursday, marking its lowest level since late 2024, and has been trading around $59,000. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded net outflows for six consecutive days, totaling $696 million on June 25, with spot Ethereum ETFs also experiencing significant outflows.
title: Higher US Inflation Dampens Rate Cut Hopes, Bitcoin Falls Below $60K

details: Piero Cipollone, a member of the European Central Bank's Executive Board, stated that the digital euro is designed to have minimal effects on European banks and will not pose a risk to financial stability. Key design features include no interest payments to holders, individual holding limits, and a 'reverse waterfall' mechanism to convert excess digital euro holdings back into bank deposits, all aimed at safeguarding bank liquidity.
title: ECB Official States Digital Euro's Impact on Banks Will Be Minimal

details: A Wall Street Journal report, based on blockchain data, revealed that Iranian entities moved over $3.84 billion in cryptocurrency through the Seychelles-based exchange CoinEx over the past six years. CoinEx reportedly became the largest foreign counterparty to Iran's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, Nobitex, after Binance tightened its sanctions compliance. This highlights the ongoing challenges authorities face in enforcing sanctions within blockchain-based financial systems.
sourceName: Iran International (citing The Wall Street Journal)
title: Iranian Entities Used CoinEx for Billions in Crypto Transfers Despite Sanctions
